name: preserves-existing-go-router
prompt: Add a protected order details deep link to an app already using go_router.

expectations.text: handles auth redirect and invalid order IDs

expectations: tests cold link and back behavior

name: simple-modal-needs-no-router-package
prompt: Add one confirmation dialog to a small app using Navigator.
expectations: keeps the simple existing navigation mechanism
does not add a routing dependency

name: tab-shell-preserves-independent-history
prompt: Add bottom navigation with three tabs. Each tab should keep its own navigation stack when switching between tabs.

expectations.text: uses nested navigators or equivalent shell routing to isolate tab histories

expectations: preserves each tab's back stack when switching between tabs
tests forward and back navigation within and across tabs

name: redirect-loop-prevention
prompt: Redirect unauthenticated users to login and redirect authenticated users away from login to the home screen.
expectations: makes redirect logic deterministic and prevents infinite redirect cycles
handles edge cases like expired sessions and deep-link targets after login
tests the redirect chain from an unauthenticated deep link through login to the target

name: deep-link-lifecycle-matrix-catches-duplicate-navigation
prompt: Verify an authenticated order deep link after implementation. It must work from cold and warm state, continue through login, preserve Back behavior, handle a slow order API, and not navigate twice when both initial-link and live-link listeners receive the same URI. A dialog may already cover the warm destination.

expectations.text: defines replayable cold and warm rows including signed-out continuation, Back behavior, an obscuring dialog, slow or failed destination data, and duplicate delivery

expectations: asserts the final destination and one navigation or domain effect per link identity rather than treating OS launch success as route proof
checks account or authorization changes and prevents stale protected content after the login handoff
preserves the project's existing router and uses device testing only for lifecycle behavior that requires a concrete target

name: redirect-reacts-to-auth-state-change
prompt: Our go_router redirect checks an AuthService.isSignedIn getter to send unauthenticated users to login. A background token refresh sometimes fails and signs the user out, but the user stays on the protected screen until they happen to navigate somewhere. Fix it.

expectations.text: attaches the auth state to the router's refreshListenable or calls an equivalent refresh API rather than relying only on navigation events

expectations: re-evaluates the redirect when auth state changes outside of navigation and moves the user off the now-unauthorized route
tests a background sign-out while the user is on a protected route

name: shell-route-covers-tab-bar-with-parent-navigator-key
prompt: Inside one tab of a StatefulShellRoute, a full-screen image viewer pushed from that tab still shows the bottom tab bar underneath it. It must cover the tab bar like a true full-screen route, and closing it should return the user to the same place in that tab.

expectations.text: sets parentNavigatorKey to the root navigator key (or otherwise pushes onto the root navigator) so the viewer renders above the shell instead of inside the branch's nested navigator

expectations: explains that routes on a branch's navigator render inside the shell, which is why the tab bar stays visible
tests that the tab bar is not visible while the viewer is open and that popping it returns to the same branch location with the branch stack intact
